#                   excluded per arm printed beside the reads: "oracle-exposed cells excluded" (a row
#                   whose oracle_exposed_defects or oracle_exposed_unknown is non-empty leaves its cell

# the primary version only; every other version gets "## Suite version N (batches: …) —
# reported separately, never pooled" with its own decision table, H1 and A4 lines, per-arm
# figures and exclusions. The header lists each version with its batches and manifest sha256
# (DRIFT is more than one sha256 within one version). A row without suite_version among rows of
# two or more versions → exit 2 when it would enter a cell; one that would be listed anyway (no

head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1913 — a0_bare_fable becomes a decision "component". It is a no-mount BARE baseline (A0 on the review model), not a removable Loa component, yet arm_report compares it with a1_full and gives it a keep/remove/simplify/investigate decision for a shipped default. The existing filter keeps a0_bare out for exactly this reason. The expected-false-positive count k goes up to 9 because of it. Exclude baseline arms (e.g. loa_mount: false / phases [BARE]) the same way BARE is excluded, and report them as a separate H1-style contrast.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:653 — the three review-catch-only arms are now components, and primaries() gives them [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate] because REVIEW is in their task_types. Such an arm never has build rows, so the pass-rate comparison always has n = 0 and is not usable. decide() then takes the "no valid pair" branch, so remove and simplify can never be reached and `decidable` is always false. a1_review_only ("drop the AUDIT gate") and a1_no_dissent can therefore never produce the decision they exist to inform. The primaries need to follow the arm's applicable task types.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:2003 — the eval_only arm is dropped from the component list, and nothing else picks it up. a1_full_openmount is missing from the Decisions table, from Per-arm detail (detail_arms), from the cap sensitivity rows, and from the oracle-exposed / dissent-absent sensitivity rows (line 1683). Only a bare open_reported row count is left. The open-mount oracle A/B, which is the only reason this arm runs, is reported nowhere. It needs a non-deciding section (or a detail entry) instead of silent omission.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:117 — the pre-registered rules block (D-A5, "mirrored in NOTES before the first run", quoted verbatim in the report's Method section) still says "expected false positives at 0.90 over 6 components printed". The report now prints 9 components. The PR changes the pre-registered multiple-comparison basis without updating or re-registering the rule.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:55 — `priority` (run-ablation.sh's default --arms) does not include any of the four new arms, but the report now always counts three of them as components. Every default batch's report therefore shows three "no rows for this arm" decisions and an EFP sentence over 9 components, 3 of which were never run. The same 9 components are also applied to the suite_version 1 partition (head/evals/tests/ablation-report.bats:342 now expects 9 decisions for v1, which predates these arms).
head/evals/tests/ablation-report.bats:189 — the expected strings were just re-baselined to the new count. The comment calls a0_bare_fable/a1_review_only/a1_no_dissent "the three cycle-131 control arms", while the code treats them as decision components. No test checks that the eval_only arm is excluded from decisions or still reported, or how a review-catch-only component is decided. The contradiction in the comment shows the design question was never settled.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:341 — the dry-run `config_edits` line is a second, hand-copied version of lib/sandbox-mount.sh apply_arm_toggles' .loa.config.yaml edits (companion_voice/gates/dissent/flatline). It reads the raw suite toggles, not the library-resolved toggles that the real run uses. Nothing ties the two together, so the dry-run can describe a sandbox config the run never applies (toggles such as karpathy_block/rule_files/audit_delta_instruction are not shown at all). The edits should come from the library (e.g. a dry-run or "describe" mode of apply_arm_toggles), not from a copy.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:259 — the eval_only guard is only an env check that any caller can satisfy (`LOA_ABLATION_BATCH_CONTEXT=1 pipeline-run.sh …`, and the header itself recommends doing this for dry runs). Nothing records that a run happened outside a run-ablation batch. Accepting this for an evaluation-only open-mount arm should be a deliberate choice. At minimum, record the context in pipeline.json/arm evidence so a manually launched open-mount run can be told apart in reporting.
